stage1_evidence_shown.label: BACKGROUND
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Embolisation of atherosclerotic debris during abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) repair is responsible for significant peri-operative morbidity. Reports have suggested that preferential clamping of the distal vessel(s) before the proximal aorta may decrease the number of emboli passing distally and hence reduce complications.

stage1_evidence_shown.label: METHODS
stage1_evidence_shown.context: Forty patients undergoing AAA repair were randomised to have either first clamping of the proximal aorta or the iliac vessels. Emboli passing through the Superficial Femoral Arteries were detected with a Transcranial Doppler ultrasound system.

stage1_model_output.raw: {"action":"ANSWER","answer":"maybe","confidence":0.25,"reason_for_action":"A randomized trial comparing proximal-first vs distal-first clamping in 40 patients is described, but no results or outcome data are provided here, so effect on distal embolisation is undetermined."}

parsed.reason_for_action: A randomized trial comparing proximal-first vs distal-first clamping in 40 patients is described, but no results or outcome data are provided here, so effect on distal embolisation is undetermined.

stage2_added_evidence.label: RESULTS
stage2_added_evidence.context: There was no difference between the two groups in the number of emboli detected (p=0.49) and no significant correlation between number of emboli and dissection time (r=0.0008). However, there was a significantly higher number of emboli in the patient sub-group that were current smokers (p=0.034).
